questions.prompt: Which load-balancing algorithm distributes requests based on the client IP so the same client consistently hits the same backend?
questions.explanation: IP hash maps each client IP to a backend deterministically, giving session affinity. Round robin and least-connections do not guarantee the same backend each time.

questions.prompt: A cache is using write-through. What happens to write latency?
options: Writes get faster because the cache absorbs them
Writes pay the cost of updating both cache and storage
Writes are acknowledged before storage, risking data loss
Writes are batched and applied asynchronously
questions.explanation: Write-through updates the cache and the underlying storage on every write, so each write pays both costs. The data-loss risk belongs to write-back, and batching is not part of write-through.
